summary: Transitioning from the Daniel series, Steve opens a short series on prayer, landing this week in 1 John 5:14-15: if we ask anything according to God's will, He hears us. Building on earlier looks at prayer in James and in Daniel's own example, the message centers on three points about what makes prayer truly purposeful. Listen in for Steve's full walkthrough of what those three points mean for how we pray.
takeaways: Prayer is a powerful, underutilized tool. It should be our first choice, not our last resort, and most of us underuse it because we don't see immediate results from skipping it.

There is no secret formula for answered prayer. The real condition in 1 John 5:14 is asking according to God's will, not ours; an unanswered prayer is not proof of insufficient faith. A real correction of the "name it and claim it" misreading of Matthew 7:7-8. Some teach that faith alone guarantees you get what you ask for. Scripture never promises that, and it isn't the case.
Proper prayer is personal, meaningful, sincere, and humble, not rote repetition or performance. God knows the posture of your heart even when you can't find the words.

Corporate prayer, the church praying together for the same things, is the most effective prayer there is. The early church grew from 18 people to 120 to 3,000 while staying prayerfully united around one mission.
